text: Based on the evidence, tree-cover loss of about 13.5 hectares occurred within this native forest asset in 2025, as detected by the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset. However, this does not conclusively establish deforestation, as the change could be due to natural causes (e.g., fire, storm) or management activities (e.g., harvesting). The observation is pending corroboration because it is the latest year in the series, and further monitoring would be needed to confirm persistence. The area was confirmed as native forest (not planted) by MGAP’s 2021 map, but the legality or intent behind the loss remains unclear. No additional data confirms whether this was permanent deforestation or temporary disturbance.
